- When sentiment is high (≥0.8) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is high, apply downward bias of 3–7% to reflect pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast 2–3 days after peak at 10–15% below peak.  
- Mean reversion is strong in late cycle — if price is above 85% of 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 2–5% per day.  
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lag — if sentiment is neutral or declining, delay peak forecast by 1–2 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), use 3-day moving average of true values to smooth forecast.
